newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bond dip seen bottoming out after US tumble.
newsitem.headline: Danish bond dip seen bottoming out after US tumble.

text.p: Danish bond prices opened lower on Monday, hit by Friday's solid decline on Wall Street and dealers described the market undertone as negative but said they saw the falls bottoming out.
"The general tone is not positive after Friday's big U.S. fall, but we reckon the falls have almost bottomed out here," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 traded 0.47 point down from Friday's close at 113.48 at 0720 GMT, yielding 5.94 percent, while the forthcoming seven pct 2007 benchmark was 0.52 point lower,at 106.43, with the yield at 6.13 percent.
The 2007's 10-year yield gap with Germany widened two basis points to 52 since Friday's close. The crown was virtually unaltered at 3.8103 per mark.
